styles.d: The foundation of every style: Disney Dancing (pre-ballet) through Ballet V, plus Pointe.
styles.more:
## Levels
- Disney Dancing: pre-ballet to favorite Disney songs
- Ballet Basics: positions, terms and short combinations, a little barre
- Combo and Ballet I to V: technique builds level by level
- Pre Pointe, Pointe I & II: ankle strength and control, then pointe work
## Good to know
- The instructor places each dancer in a level
- Pre Pointe: in Ballet II or III, plus one more ballet class
- Pointe I: a year of Pre Pointe and in Ballet III or IV
## What to wear
- Solid black leotard, studio brand tights; skirt or tutu optional for Disney Dancing
- Ballet I: studio brand ballet shoes. Ballet I/II and up: So Danca or Capezio canvas
- Tight ballet bun, bangs away from face

styles.d: Jazz Hip Hop (ages 6+), Jazz II–III and Jazz/Lyrical I–III.
styles.more:
## Levels
- Jazz Hip Hop I and I/II (ages 6+): beginner jazz technique and body movement
- Jazz II and III: intermediate to advanced technique
- Jazz/Lyrical I to III: jazz technique plus lyrical, telling a song’s story through movement
## Good to know
- The instructor places each dancer in a level
- Jazz/Lyrical needs a ballet class too
## What to wear
- Solid black leotard, tight shorts or leggings (boys: black shirt and shorts)
- Jazz Hip Hop: black jazz shoes. Jazz/Lyrical: studio brand tan jazz shoes
- Bun or ponytail, bangs away from face

## Levels
- Tiny Tap (ages 3–5): first steps and sing-along songs
- Tap Basics (ages 5+): simple rhythms
- Tap I to IV: rhythms and sounds get more complex each level
## What to wear
- Solid black leotard, tight shorts or leggings (boys: black shirt and shorts)
- Studio brand tap shoes. Tap 2 & 3: studio premium tap shoes. Tap 4: Capezio Tan Manhattan Xtreme heel
- Bun or ponytail, bangs away from face

styles.d: Hip Hop Basics (ages 4+) through Hip Hop III.
styles.more:
## Levels
- Hip Hop Basics (ages 4+): rhythm, first steps and sing-alongs
- Hip Hop I (ages 7+) to III: hip hop culture and technique, beginner to advanced
## What to wear
- Basics: black leotard with shorts or leggings. Hip Hop I and up: loose, comfortable clothes (no jeans or belts)
- Clean gym shoes worn only inside (change at the studio)

styles.d: Intro to Breaking (ages 6+) and Breaking I & II.
styles.more:
## Levels
- Intro to Breaking (ages 6+): basics that build rhythm, strength, flexibility and focus
- Breaking I & II: twice a week; footwork, freezes and harder steps with conditioning
## Good to know
- Breaking is an Olympic sport now
- The Breaking I & II combined class is included with Breaking I or II
## What to wear
- Loose, comfortable clothes (no jeans or belts)
- Clean gym shoes worn only inside
- A spin cap, bought from The Breaking Program at the studio

## Levels
- Acro Basics (ages 4+): rolls, cartwheels, bridges and balance
- Acro I (ages 6+) to II: tumbling and balancing skills build each level
## What to wear
- Any color leotard, tight shorts or leggings
- Barefoot
- Hair pulled back

## Levels
- Modern/Contemporary I (ages 8+) to III: modern technique with contemporary movement
- Contemporary: jazz, ballet and modern skills for free-form expression
## Good to know
- Modern/Contemporary needs a ballet class too
## What to wear
- Modern/Contemporary: any color leotard, shorts or leggings; barefoot
- Contemporary: solid black leotard, shorts or leggings; half sole shoes
- Hair pulled back, bangs away from face

styles.d: Sing, act and dance: Musical Theater I to III.
styles.more:
## Levels
- Musical Theater I to III: jazz technique with storytelling, acting and character work
## What to wear
- Solid black leotard, tight shorts or leggings (boys: black shirt and shorts)
- Studio brand tan jazz shoes
- Tight bun, bangs away from face

styles.d: Mommy/Daddy & Me for babies and toddlers.
styles.more:
Move together and build motor skills in a fun class.
## Good to know

texts.introBody: From a first plié to the thrill of performance, we create space for dancers to grow with strong technique, expressive movement, and a community that moves together.
texts.story: Brittany Brady opened Dance & All That Jazz in Prospect Heights in 2013 with eight classes a week. Today there are three studio spaces and more than 70 classes a week, and a community where dance, performance and competition thrive together.
texts.companyIntro: More than a competitive team, Company is where dancers grow. It’s an audition-based program for dancers who are driven, open to challenge and ready to represent Dance & All That Jazz with pride, with yearly performances and 3–4 regional competitions from March to May.
texts.auditions: Company is an audition-based team for dancers ready to work hard and grow. Dancers must be 7 by September 1. Placement is based on attitude, technique, performance and readiness for the commitment.
texts.auditionsMore:
## When
- New Member Auditions: Sunday, January 17, 2027 (sign up by January 15)
- Returning Company Member Auditions: June 14–18, 2027, during Summer Intensives week
More than a competitive team: Company dancers represent the studio and grow as people.
## Who can audition
- 7 years old by September 1
- New dancers also take the Summer Intensive Week and the Summer Dance Session
## Classes you need first
- Petite (Combo / Ballet I level), 2 classes: a full 55-minute Ballet or Combo, plus Jazz Lyrical, Jazz Hip Hop, Combo, Tap or Musical Theater
- Intermediate, Junior, Teen & Senior (Ballet I/II and up), 3 classes: Ballet; Modern/Contemporary or Jazz Lyrical; plus Jazz Hip Hop, Hip Hop, Tap or Musical Theater
## What we look for
- Dedicated, prepared and hardworking
- Positive leaders and supportive teammates
- Open to challenge and feedback, proud to represent D&ATJ
## What Company dancers gain
- Confidence, strong technique and artistry
- Time management and accountability
- A team that feels like family
- Performances plus 3–4 regional competitions, March to May

texts.losIntro: Dance education scholarships for Dance & All That Jazz students.
texts.losStory:
The Light On Stage Foundation was established in December 2023 by Dance & All That Jazz Founder and Studio Owner, Brittany Brady, in loving memory of Kat Koziara, one of our beloved Breaking students and student instructors, who tragically lost her life in a car accident.

Kat was truly a light on stage, bringing joy, passion, and energy to every performance. Her love for dance and the impact she made on our studio community continue to inspire us.

To honor Kat’s memory and keep her light shining, the foundation provides dance education scholarships to children and families experiencing financial hardships. Our mission is to ensure that financial challenges never prevent a child from experiencing the joy of dance.

Through the Light On Stage Foundation, Kat’s light continues to shine, giving more children the opportunity to dance, grow, and follow their passion.
texts.losGiveNote: Every gift goes to dance education scholarships for D&ATJ families experiencing financial hardship.

staff.name: Brittany Brady
staff.bio:
Brittany Brady (Cederberg) is the founder and CEO of Dance & All That Jazz Studio, which she established in 2013.
Brittany’s passion for dance began at the young age of four, quickly growing into a lifelong love. She continued to dance throughout high school and later attended Illinois State University, where she was a member of the Redline Dance Team. Brittany pursued her passion by majoring in Business Entrepreneurship & Management with a minor in Dance Performance. Even as a little girl, Brittany had a clear vision for her future. Before heading off to college, she noticed a newly constructed strip mall in her hometown of Prospect Heights. She confidently told her parents that she would one day open her dance studio there.
After graduating from college, Brittany continued to teach dance while working at a bank. Despite her success in banking, the dream of opening a dance studio never faded. In 2013, Brittany took the leap and fulfilled her dream, launching Dance & All That Jazz Studio with just eight classes a week. By 2016, Brittany’s vision had expanded, leading her to take over an additional space next to her studio. The studio expanded again in 2022, with the opening of a third studio space, now offering more than 70 classes a week.
Brittany is grateful for the supportive community that has grown around Dance & All That Jazz. She is committed to maintaining a welcoming environment where dance, performance, and competition can thrive together. At Dance & All That Jazz, dancers not only learn to dance but also pick up valuable life skills and build meaningful friendships.

staff.name: Katie Carey
staff.bio: Katie Carey, has dedicated her life to the art of dance. With a passion that started at a young age in her hometown of Columbus, Ohio she moved to Chicago to train with Giordano Dance Chicago. Katie has performed as a main company dancer with Nomi Dance Company and Cocodaco Dance Project. Through her performances and choreography, she creates from the idea of letting a moment with someone on something take over until you give in completely with an abandonment to the feeling. Whether it be love, heartache, excitement, passion or grief, let it shake you to your core. She calls this concept “method dancing”. Katie is the co-founder of Purus Motus, a company that produces dance cinema, and is dedicated to merging concert dance and hip hop to create a unique viewpoint into how we watch different styles of dance. Purus Motus has been selected to present their work at film festivals around the world. Most recently they premiered at the San Francisco Film Festival. Katie has had the opportunity to create works on Nomi Dance Company, Trifecta Dance Collective, Cocodaco Dance Project, New Dances, Moonwater Dance Project, and is currently the resident choreographer for Hot Crowd, a contemporary/modern dance company in Chicago. In addition to her choreography career, Katie has been actively involved in teaching dance. She has conducted workshops and choreographed award winning dances all over the Midwest. Katie is immensely grateful for this life of constant creativity and is excited for the future!

staff.name: Kelly Cunningham
staff.bio: Kelly began dancing at age 3 and has continued to feel a strong love and passion for dance ever since. She grew up in Cary, IL where she studied dance, voice, and acting her entire life. Her dance training includes jazz, tap, lyrical, ballet, hip hop, and musical theater styles. Kelly has trained with the Goodman Theater as well as getting her BFA in musical theater from Millikin University, and performing professional theater with William Street Rep. While at Millikin, Kelly was awarded with the Ron Smith Award for excellence in Musical Theater. Kelly believes in the power that art can have in our lives. How it teaches us not only about ourselves but the world around us, and how we can use art to encourage our differences and tell stories that spark conversation and change. She loves that being a teacher and choreographer allows her to instill that appreciation for dance as an art form to her students.

staff.name: Meghan Hutto
staff.bio: Meghan Hutto is from Richmond, Virginia, where she began her dance training at Premiere Dance Studio. In high school, she completed a traineeship at the School of Richmond Ballet. In 2025, she graduated with honors from Butler University with a degree in Dance Performance and Computer Science. She has been a soloist in numerous choreography projects created by her peers and professors at Butler, as well as performing many full-length ballets. She has attended many workshops with Alvin Ailey, Hubbard Street, Steps on Broadway, and Visceral Dance Chicago. Additionally, she performed in Jamboree, a professional choreography workshop held by WhirlWind. Currently, she is a trainee with Visceral Dance Chicago. Her Inspiration comes from other artists’ passion and love for dance, and she is excited to be part of the Dance & All That Jazz community!

staff.name: Allison Pauley
staff.bio: Allison Pauley is a dance artist hailing from Buffalo Grove, IL. In May 2016, she graduated from the University of Illinois with a Bachelor of Fine Arts in Dance. At U of I, she had the pleasure of performing in works by faculty members Jan Erkert, Kristie Simson, Abby Zibikowski, and Sara Hook, as well as guest artists Jennifer Archibald and Earl Mosley. Her junior year, Pauley attended the Jerusalem Academy of Dance where she trained in Gaga with Batsheva Company.

staff.name: Daniel Williams
staff.bio: With over a decade long of teaching experience in street art, Daniel has made a very unconventional style of learning hip hop very popular. Coming from the underground scene of hip hop, bboying, popping, and house, Daniel makes sure these styles are brought to the forefront of his choreography. Daniel has trained or worked under the influences of Brickheadz crew, Chicago Dance Crash, Shadow Puppets, and countless individuals to cultivate an array of bounce, groove, rock, roll and hit techniques to advance the complexity of the movement forward in the classroom.

staff.name: Dillon Zamora
staff.bio: Dillon Zamora is a Chicago-based dance performer and choreographer. Dillon trained at his home studio in California in the Cecchetti Ballet method, contemporary, jazz, and hip hop. Dillon later studied at the University of California Irvine where he received two BFAs for Dance Choreography and Dance Performance. While at UCI Dillon performed in multiple shows and performed in works by Lar Lubovitch and Vitor Luiz DeSantos. Dillon was a trainee with Visceral Dance Chicago and worked with Braeden Barnes, Tina Diaz, Nick Pupillo, and Cait Cucchiarra. He’s also had the opportunity to work with renowned choreographers such as Ethan Colangelo, Nicole Von Arx, Alex Ketley, and Nicole Hennington. Currently, Dillon is a company dancer for both Winifred Haun and Dancers under the direction of Winifred Haun, and The Seldoms under the direction of Carrie Hanson.

staff.name: Ben Goodman
staff.bio: Ben started dancing at Dance & All That Jazz 10 years ago as a student, and now he’s back as an instructor. He’s spent the past 3 years in Indianapolis as an NBA dancer for the Indiana Pacers as well as a breakdance instructor. His favorite thing about teaching breakdance is that it’s a fun space to be creative and try new things.

staff.name: Shetal Lettvin
staff.bio: Dancing has been a part of Shetal's life for as long as she can remember. She began performing at family events as a child and officially started dancing at the age of six. Growing up immersed in Bollywood music and culture, dance quickly became a natural form of expression for her. She was a member of the Poms team throughout middle and high school, and later in college, she joined and led a competitive Bollywood dance team that performed at events across the country. Outside of dance, she works in the sustainability industry and stay on her toes raising three energetic young kids!

staff.name: Akanksha Patel
staff.bio: With a lifelong love of dance, Akanksha brings a rich and versatile background to the studio. Classically trained in Kathak, she has also studied a wide range of Western styles including ballet, tap, jazz, hip hop, and contemporary. In high school, she was a member of her varsity poms team, and in college, she continued dancing as part of a Bollywood fusion team, blending traditional Indian dance with Western choreography. Akanksha continues to fuel her enthusiasm for movement by training with traveling choreographers in Indian-inspired styles. She’s excited to share her passion for Bollywood fusion and looks forward to bringing energy, creativity, and joy to every class!
